key_moments.description: Xerxes held a great feast in Shushan the palace. On its seventh day, when he was merry with wine, he sent for Queen Vashti to show off her beauty, but she refused, and he burned with anger.
key_moments.title: Defied by Queen Vashti

key_moments.description: The king loved Esther more than all the other women and put the royal crown on her head in place of Vashti. Then he held a great feast for his princes and servants, called Esther's feast.
key_moments.title: Crowns Esther Queen

key_moments.description: Haman told the king of a people whose laws were different and offered silver to have them destroyed. The king gave Haman his ring and let him deal with the people as he liked.
key_moments.title: Gives Haman His Ring

key_moments.description: One night the king could not sleep, so he had the records read to him. He heard how Mordecai had exposed a plot to kill him, and learned that nothing had been done to honor him.
key_moments.title: Hears How Mordecai Saved Him

key_moments.description: When Esther pleaded for her life and her people, the king asked who had dared to do this. She named Haman, and the king had him hanged on the gallows he had built for Mordecai.
key_moments.title: Has Haman Hanged

name: Xerxes
summary: A king who reigned over 127 provinces, from India to Ethiopia, from his throne in Shushan the palace. He put away Queen Vashti, made Esther his queen, and turned against Haman when Esther revealed his plot.

key_moments.description: After the angel's promise to Zechariah, Elizabeth became pregnant and stayed hidden for five months. She said the Lord had taken away her shame among people.
key_moments.title: Conceives in Her Old Age

key_moments.description: When Mary greeted her, the baby leaped inside Elizabeth and the Holy Ghost filled her. She called Mary blessed among women and the mother of her Lord.
key_moments.title: Feels Her Baby Leap at Mary's Greeting

key_moments.description: Elizabeth gave birth to a son, and her neighbours rejoiced with her. When they wanted to name him after his father, she said he would be called John.
key_moments.title: Naming Her Son John

name: Elizabeth
summary: A woman descended from Aaron, married to the priest Zechariah, who had no children into old age. God gave her a son, John, and when Mary visited, she was filled with the Holy Ghost and blessed her.

key_moments.description: While Zechariah burned incense in the temple, an angel appeared beside the altar. The angel told him his prayer was heard and Elizabeth would bear him a son named John.
key_moments.title: Visited by an Angel at the Altar

key_moments.description: Zechariah asked how he could know this, since he and his wife were old. Gabriel said that because he did not believe, he would not be able to speak until it happened, and he came out unable to talk.
key_moments.title: Struck Dumb for Not Believing

key_moments.description: When the baby was eight days old, Zechariah asked for a writing tablet and wrote that his name was John. At once he could speak again, and he praised God.
key_moments.title: Writing the Name John

key_moments.description: Filled with the Holy Ghost, Zechariah blessed God for coming to save His people. He said his son would be called the prophet of the Highest and go before the Lord to prepare His ways.
key_moments.title: Zechariah Prophesies

name: Zechariah
summary: A priest who, with his wife Elizabeth, had no children into old age. The angel Gabriel told him he would have a son, John, and because he did not believe, he could not speak until the boy was named.

key_moments.description: Elizabeth gave birth to a son in her old age. Neighbours wanted to name him after his father, but she said he would be called John, and Zechariah wrote the same.
key_moments.title: Named John

key_moments.description: John preached in the wilderness of Judaea, telling people to repent because heaven's kingdom was near. He wore camel's hair, ate locusts and honey from the wild, and baptized people in the Jordan.
key_moments.title: Preaches in the Wilderness

key_moments.description: Jesus came to be baptized, and John said he needed to be baptized by Jesus instead. When Jesus came up from the water, the Spirit came down like a dove and a voice from heaven spoke.
key_moments.title: Baptizing Jesus

key_moments.description: Seeing Jesus coming toward him, John called Him the Lamb of God who takes away the world's sin. The next day two of John's disciples heard him and followed Jesus.
key_moments.title: Calls Jesus the Lamb of God

key_moments.description: John told Herod it was not lawful for him to have his brother's wife, so Herod put him in prison. At Herod's birthday feast, the daughter of Herodias asked for John's head, and Herod had him beheaded.
key_moments.title: Beheaded by Herod

name: John
summary: The son of Zechariah and Elizabeth, sent by God to prepare the way for Jesus. He preached repentance, baptized people in the Jordan, and pointed others to Jesus as the Lamb of God.

key_moments.description: When Esther's turn came to go to the king, she won the favor of all who saw her. The king loved her more than all the other women and put the royal crown on her head in place of Vashti.
key_moments.title: Made Queen

key_moments.description: Esther asked all the Jews in Shushan to fast for her three days and nights, and said she and her maidens would fast too. Then she would go in to the king, against the law, even if it cost her life.
key_moments.title: Calls a Three-Day Fast

key_moments.description: Three days later Esther stood in the king's inner court, and he held out his golden sceptre to her. She invited the king and Haman to a banquet she had prepared.
key_moments.title: Goes In to the King

key_moments.description: At her next banquet Esther asked the king for her life and the lives of her people, who had been sold to be destroyed. When the king asked who had done this, she said it was this wicked Haman.
key_moments.title: Names Haman as the Enemy

key_moments.description: Queen Esther and Mordecai wrote with full authority to confirm the days of Purim. Esther's decree settled these matters, and it was recorded.
key_moments.title: Confirms the Days of Purim

name: Esther
summary: Esther was a Jewish orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai who became queen to King Xerxes. She risked her life to go before the king and saved her people from Haman's plot to destroy them.

key_moments.description: As Mordecai sat at the king's gate, he learned that two of the king's doorkeepers planned to kill King Xerxes. He told Esther, she told the king in Mordecai's name, and the matter was recorded in the king's chronicles.
key_moments.title: Saving the King's Life

key_moments.description: The king's servants bowed to Haman as the king had commanded, but Mordecai would not. He had told them he was Jewish, and Haman, full of anger, set out to destroy all of Mordecai's people.
key_moments.title: Refuses to Bow to Haman

key_moments.description: Mordecai warned Esther that she would be no safer in the palace than the other Jews. He asked who knew whether she had become queen for this very time.
key_moments.title: Tells Esther Not to Keep Silent

key_moments.description: The king told Haman to dress Mordecai in royal clothes and lead him on the king's horse. So Haman brought him through the city, crying out that this was how the king honored a man.
key_moments.title: Honored Through the City

key_moments.description: After Haman was hanged, the king gave Mordecai the ring taken back from Haman. Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's house.
key_moments.title: Given the King's Ring

name: Mordecai
summary: Mordecai was a Jew of the tribe of Benjamin in Shushan who raised his cousin Esther as his own daughter. He would not bow to Haman, urged Esther to plead for her people, and rose to be next to the king.

key_moments.description: The angel Gabriel told Mary she had found favour with God and would bear a son named Jesus. She asked how this could be, then called herself the Lord's handmaid and agreed.
key_moments.title: Told She Will Bear Jesus

key_moments.description: Mary hurried to see her cousin Elizabeth, and Elizabeth's baby leaped at her greeting. Mary praised the Lord and stayed about three months.
key_moments.title: Visiting Elizabeth

key_moments.description: In Bethlehem Mary gave birth to her firstborn son and placed Him in a manger. When the shepherds came, she treasured all of this and thought it over in her heart.
key_moments.title: Gives Birth to Jesus in Bethlehem

key_moments.description: Mary stood near the cross of Jesus. Seeing her and the disciple He loved, Jesus gave them to each other as mother and son.
key_moments.title: Stands at the Cross

key_moments.description: After Jesus was taken up, Mary the mother of Jesus prayed together with the apostles, the women and His brothers in Jerusalem.
key_moments.title: Praying With the Disciples

name: Mary
summary: A virgin of Nazareth, engaged to Joseph, whom the angel Gabriel told she would bear the Son of God. She gave birth to Jesus in Bethlehem and stood by His cross.

key_moments.description: Dorcas, a woman full of good works and gifts to the poor, fell sick and died. The disciples sent for Peter, and the weeping widows showed him the coats and clothes she had made.
key_moments.title: Mourned by the Widows

key_moments.description: Peter sent everyone out, knelt and prayed, and told Tabitha to rise. She looked up, saw Peter and sat up, and he presented her alive. Word of it spread through all Joppa, and many people put their faith in the Lord.
key_moments.title: Raised from the Dead

name: Dorcas
summary: A disciple at Joppa, also called Tabitha, who was known for her good works and her gifts to the poor. When she died, Peter prayed and called her to rise, and she came back to life.

key_moments.description: Leah bore Jacob a sixth son and said God had given her a good dowry, and now her husband would dwell with her. She named him Zebulun.
key_moments.title: Born to Leah

key_moments.description: Zebulun went down to Egypt with his father Jacob and the whole family, along with his sons.
key_moments.title: Goes Down to Egypt

key_moments.description: Jacob said Zebulun would live at the haven of the sea and be a haven for ships, with his border reaching to Zidon.
key_moments.title: Blessed by Jacob

name: Zebulun
summary: Jacob's sixth son by Leah. Jacob said Zebulun would live by the sea and be a haven for ships.

key_moments.description: Amos begged the Lord GOD to spare Jacob, and twice the LORD held back. Then Amos saw the Lord holding a plumbline, which He would set among His people Israel.
key_moments.title: Begs the LORD to Spare Jacob

key_moments.description: Amaziah the priest of Bethel told Amos to flee to Judah. Amos answered that he was no prophet, just a herdsman who gathered sycamore fruit, but the LORD had sent him to prophesy.
key_moments.title: Told to Leave Bethel

key_moments.description: The LORD showed Amos a basket of ripe summer fruit and told him the end had come for His people Israel.
key_moments.title: Shown a Basket of Summer Fruit

name: Amos
summary: A herdsman from Tekoa whom the LORD called away from his flock to prophesy to Israel. He saw visions of judgment and stood firm when the priest of Bethel told him to leave.

key_moments.description: The Lord told Ananias in a vision to go to the street called Straight and find Saul of Tarsus, who was praying. Ananias said he had heard of the evil Saul had done, but the Lord said Saul was His chosen vessel to carry His name to the Gentiles.
key_moments.title: Called in a Vision

key_moments.description: Ananias went in, laid his hands on Saul, and called him brother, saying Jesus had sent him so that Saul could see again and the Holy Ghost would fill him. Something like scales fell from Saul's eyes, and he could see, and he was baptized.
key_moments.title: Lays His Hands on Saul

name: Ananias
summary: A devout disciple in Damascus whom the Lord sent to Saul after Saul lost his sight. Though he had heard of the evil Saul had done, he obeyed, laid his hands on him, and Saul could see again.

key_moments.description: Apollos, an eloquent Jew from Alexandria who knew the scriptures well, arrived in Ephesus. He was fervent in spirit and taught carefully about the Lord, though he knew only the baptism of John.
key_moments.title: Preaches Boldly in Ephesus

key_moments.description: Apollos was preaching boldly in the synagogue. When Aquila and Priscilla heard him, they took him in and explained the way of God to him more fully.
key_moments.title: Taught by Aquila and Priscilla

key_moments.description: The brethren wrote ahead asking the disciples in Achaia to welcome Apollos. There he greatly helped the believers, and he showed the Jews publicly from the scriptures that Jesus was the Christ.
key_moments.title: Helps the Believers in Achaia

name: Apollos
summary: A Jew born at Alexandria, a gifted speaker who knew the scriptures well. After Aquila and Priscilla taught him more, he greatly helped the believers, and Paul called him a fellow servant who watered what Paul had planted.

key_moments.description: Joses, a Levite from Cyprus whom the apostles named Barnabas, sold his land and brought the money to the apostles. The believers shared like this so that no one among them was in need.
key_moments.title: Giving Away His Land

key_moments.description: When Saul came to Jerusalem, the disciples were afraid of him and did not believe he was a disciple. Barnabas brought him to the apostles and told how Saul had seen the Lord and had spoken boldly in Damascus in Jesus' name.
key_moments.title: Standing Up for Saul

key_moments.description: The church in Jerusalem sent Barnabas to Antioch, where he was glad to see God's grace at work and urged the believers to hold fast to the Lord. He fetched Saul from Tarsus, they taught there for a whole year, and the disciples were first called Christians at Antioch.
key_moments.title: Sent to Antioch

key_moments.description: At Lystra, after Paul healed a man who had never walked, the crowd called Barnabas Jupiter and Paul Mercurius and wanted to offer sacrifices to them. Barnabas and Paul tore their clothes and cried out that they were only men.
key_moments.title: Mistaken for a God

key_moments.description: Barnabas wanted to take John Mark on their next journey, but Paul did not, because Mark had left them in Pamphylia. Their quarrel grew so sharp that they parted, and Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus.
key_moments.title: Parting from Paul

name: Barnabas
summary: A Levite from Cyprus named Joses, whom the apostles called Barnabas, meaning son of consolation. He stood up for Saul, encouraged the new church at Antioch, and travelled with Paul preaching to the Gentiles.

key_moments.description: Cornelius, a devout centurion of the Italian band, saw an angel of God in a vision. The angel said his prayers and gifts had come up before God and told him to send men to Joppa for Simon Peter.
key_moments.title: Visited by an Angel

key_moments.description: Cornelius gathered his relatives and close friends, and when Peter came in he fell at his feet to worship him. Peter lifted him up, saying that he too was only a man.
key_moments.title: Meeting Peter

key_moments.description: Cornelius told Peter about his vision, and Peter preached Jesus to everyone gathered there. While Peter was still speaking, the Holy Ghost came on all who heard, and they were baptized.
key_moments.title: Receives the Holy Ghost

name: Cornelius
summary: A centurion in Caesarea who feared God, gave generously and prayed always. An angel told him to send for Peter, and while Peter preached in his house, the Holy Ghost came upon the Gentiles who were listening.

key_moments.description: After Abraham said Sarah was his sister, Abimelech took her, but God warned him in a dream. Abimelech gave Sarah back with gifts, and when Abraham prayed, God healed his household.
key_moments.title: Warned in a Dream

key_moments.description: Abimelech came to Abraham, saying God was with him in all he did. They settled a quarrel over a well and swore a covenant at Beersheba.
key_moments.title: Covenant at Beersheba

key_moments.description: Isaac told the men of Gerar that Rebekah was his sister. When Abimelech saw Isaac with her, he knew she was his wife, and he warned his people not to touch either of them.
key_moments.title: Learns Rebekah Is Isaac's Wife

key_moments.description: Abimelech came from Gerar with Phichol, his army's captain, saying they had seen that the LORD was with Isaac. Isaac made them a feast, and they swore peace with each other.
key_moments.title: Peace with Isaac

name: Abimelech
summary: The king of Gerar who was told by Abraham that Sarah was his sister, and later by Isaac that Rebekah was his. Each time he made a covenant of peace with them.

key_moments.description: The lords of the Philistines each promised Delilah eleven hundred pieces of silver if she could find out what made Samson strong and how to bind him.
key_moments.title: Paid to Find His Strength

key_moments.description: Three times Samson told Delilah a false secret: seven fresh cords, new ropes, and his hair woven into a loom. Each time she called the Philistines, and each time he broke free.
key_moments.title: Deceived Three Times by Samson

key_moments.description: Delilah pressed Samson day after day until he told her the secret of his strength. She sent for the Philistine lords, had his seven locks shaved while he slept on her knees, and the Philistines seized him.
key_moments.title: Betrays Samson to the Philistines

name: Delilah
summary: A woman in the valley of Sorek whom Samson loved. The lords of the Philistines paid her to learn the secret of his strength, and she gave him into their hands.

key_moments.description: Demetrius gathered the craftsmen and warned that Paul's teaching against gods made with hands was turning people away and putting their trade in danger. They grew angry and shouted praise to Diana, and uproar spread through the whole city.
key_moments.title: Stirs Up a Riot in Ephesus

key_moments.description: The town clerk quieted the crowd and said that if Demetrius and his craftsmen had a complaint against anyone, the courts were open. He warned that they could be called to account for the riot, and he sent the crowd away.
key_moments.title: Told to Take His Case to Court

name: Demetrius
summary: A silversmith in Ephesus who made silver shrines for the goddess Diana. Warning that Paul's preaching put their trade in danger, he stirred up the craftsmen and set off an uproar in the city.

key_moments.description: When Israel did evil again, the LORD made Eglon strong against them. He joined with Ammon and Amalek, struck Israel and took the city of palm trees, and Israel served him eighteen years.
key_moments.title: Rules Over Israel Eighteen Years

key_moments.description: Eglon was sitting alone in his summer parlour when Ehud said he had a message from God for him. As Eglon rose from his seat, Ehud drove a dagger into his belly so deep that the fat closed over the blade.
key_moments.title: Stabbed by Ehud

key_moments.description: Ehud locked the parlour doors and slipped away. Eglon's servants waited outside until they were ashamed, then opened the doors with a key and found their lord dead on the floor.
key_moments.title: Found Dead by His Servants

name: Eglon
summary: A king of Moab whom the LORD made strong against Israel when they did evil, and Israel served him eighteen years. He was a very fat man, and Ehud killed him in his summer parlour.

key_moments.description: The prophet Gad told David not to stay in the stronghold but to go into the land of Judah. So David went to the forest of Hareth.
key_moments.title: Tells David to Leave the Stronghold

key_moments.description: After David numbered the people, the LORD sent Gad to offer him three things: seven years of famine, three months fleeing his enemies, or three days of plague. David chose to be punished by the LORD rather than by men, for His mercies are great.
key_moments.title: Brings David Three Choices

key_moments.description: When the LORD stopped the angel at Jerusalem, Gad told David to build an altar to the LORD at the threshing floor of Araunah. David did as Gad said and went up.
key_moments.title: Tells David to Build an Altar

name: Gad
summary: A prophet, called David's seer, who brought the LORD's word to David. He told David where to go when he was hiding from Saul, and after David numbered the people he brought the LORD's three choices and the command to build an altar.

key_moments.description: Habakkuk asked the LORD how long he must cry about violence without being heard. The LORD answered that He was raising up the Chaldeans, a bitter and hasty nation, and Habakkuk asked why God held His tongue while the wicked devoured.
key_moments.title: Asks the LORD How Long He Must Cry

key_moments.description: Habakkuk stood on his watchtower to see what the LORD would say. The LORD told him to write the vision plainly on tablets and wait for it though it tarry, for the just shall live by his faith.
key_moments.title: Told to Write the Vision Plainly

key_moments.description: Habakkuk heard the LORD and trembled. Yet he said that though the fig tree did not blossom and the fields gave no food, he would rejoice in the LORD, the God of his salvation and his strength.
key_moments.title: Rejoices in the LORD Though Crops Fail

name: Habakkuk
summary: A prophet who asked the LORD how long violence would go unpunished, waited for His answer, and ended rejoicing in the LORD though every crop should fail. Scripture tells nothing more about him and names no one else alongside him.

key_moments.description: Wise men came to Jerusalem asking where the newborn King of the Jews was, and Herod was troubled. He secretly asked them when the star appeared and sent them to Bethlehem, but God warned them in a dream not to return to him.
key_moments.title: Troubled by the Wise Men

key_moments.description: When Herod saw the wise men had tricked him, he was furious. He had all the children in and around Bethlehem aged two and under killed.
key_moments.title: Orders the Children of Bethlehem Killed

key_moments.description: After Herod died, an angel told Joseph in Egypt that those who sought the child's life were dead. Herod's son Archelaus then reigned in Judaea in his place.
key_moments.title: Dies, and Archelaus Reigns

name: Herod
summary: The king of Judaea when Jesus was born in Bethlehem. Troubled by news of a newborn King of the Jews, he tried to find and kill the child.

key_moments.description: The LORD said there was none like His servant Job on the earth. Satan answered that Job feared God only because God had blessed him, so the LORD let Satan touch all that Job had, but not Job himself.
key_moments.title: Put into Satan's Power

key_moments.description: Messenger after messenger told Job that his animals and servants were taken or killed, and that a great wind had struck the house where his children were, killing them. Job tore his robe, fell down and worshipped, and blessed the LORD's name.
key_moments.title: Loses Everything in a Day

key_moments.description: Satan covered Job with painful boils from head to foot, and he sat among the ashes. His wife urged him to curse God so he would die, but Job asked whether they should accept good from God and not trouble.
key_moments.title: Covered in Boils

key_moments.description: The LORD spoke to Job from the whirlwind. He asked Job where he was when He set the earth's foundations, as the stars of morning sang.
key_moments.title: Answered by the LORD from the Whirlwind

key_moments.description: When Job prayed for his three friends, the LORD restored him and gave him double what he had before. Again he had seven sons and three daughters, and he lived 140 more years.
key_moments.title: Blessed Twice Over

name: Job
summary: Job was a man in the land of Uz who was perfect and upright, feared God and turned away from evil. He lost his children, his wealth and his health but did not sin in what he said, and in the end the LORD gave him double what he had before.

key_moments.description: On the evening before the sabbath, Joseph went in boldly to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. Pilate was surprised Jesus was already dead, and after the centurion confirmed it, he gave the body to Joseph.
key_moments.title: Begs Pilate for Jesus' Body

key_moments.description: Joseph took the body and, with Nicodemus, wrapped it in linen with spices. They laid Jesus in Joseph's own new tomb cut out of the rock, in a garden near where He was crucified, and Joseph rolled a great stone to the door.
key_moments.title: Lays Jesus in His Own New Tomb

name: Joseph
summary: A rich man of Arimathaea and an honourable counsellor who was a disciple of Jesus, though secretly for fear of the Jews. After the crucifixion he asked Pilate for Jesus' body and laid it in his own new tomb.

key_moments.description: At a place of prayer by a river outside Philippi, Lydia heard Paul speak, and the Lord opened her heart to his words. She and her household were baptized, and she urged Paul's company to stay at her house.
key_moments.title: Baptized with Her Household

key_moments.description: When Paul and Silas were released from prison, they went to Lydia's house. There they saw the believers, encouraged them, and then left the city.
key_moments.title: Welcomes Paul and Silas After Prison

name: Lydia
summary: A seller of purple from the city of Thyatira who worshipped God. In Philippi the Lord opened her heart to Paul's message, and she was baptized with her household and opened her home to Paul and his companions.

key_moments.description: Jesus went through cities and villages preaching, with the twelve and some women He had healed. Among them was Mary Magdalene, out of whom seven devils had gone.
key_moments.title: Following Jesus

key_moments.description: Mary Magdalene and other women who had followed Jesus from Galilee watched the crucifixion from a distance. Then she saw where His body was laid.
key_moments.title: Watching at the Cross

key_moments.description: Early on the week's first day, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene came to the tomb and saw the stone had been moved away. She ran to tell Peter and the other disciple.
key_moments.title: Finds the Stone Taken Away

key_moments.description: Mary stood weeping outside the tomb. Jesus said her name, she knew Him and called Him Rabboni, meaning Master, and then she went and told the disciples about seeing the Lord and what He said.
key_moments.title: Called by Name

name: Mary Magdalene
summary: A woman out of whom Jesus cast seven devils, who followed Him and helped provide for Him. She watched His crucifixion, and she was the first to whom He appeared after He rose.

key_moments.description: When Abram came back from defeating Chedorlaomer and the kings with him, Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God most high, came out with bread and wine.
key_moments.title: Brings Bread and Wine to Abram

key_moments.description: Melchizedek blessed Abram by the most high God, maker of heaven and earth, and praised God for giving Abram victory over his enemies. Abram gave him a tenth of everything.
key_moments.title: Blesses Abram and Receives a Tenth

name: Melchisedec
summary: The king of Salem and a priest of the most high God, who met Abram with bread and wine and blessed him. Abram gave him a tenth of everything.

key_moments.description: When some widows were being neglected in the daily sharing, the church chose seven men to look after it. Stephen, a man of faith and the Holy Ghost, was the first one named.
key_moments.title: Chosen to Serve

key_moments.description: Stephen did great wonders among the people, and those who argued with him could not stand against his wisdom. They brought false witnesses against him before the council, and everyone there saw that his face looked like an angel's.
key_moments.title: Accused Before the Council

key_moments.description: Stephen saw God's glory and Jesus standing at God's right hand, and the crowd threw him out of the city and stoned him. He asked the Lord Jesus to receive his spirit and prayed that this sin would not be held against them.
key_moments.title: Stoned Outside the City

name: Stephen
summary: One of the seven chosen to serve the church, full of faith, power and the Holy Ghost, who did great wonders among the people. He was stoned after telling the council he saw Jesus standing at the right hand of God, and he prayed for those who killed him.

key_moments.description: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon besieged Jerusalem. He carried King Jehoiachin, the LORD's temple treasures and thousands of captives away to Babylon.
key_moments.title: Takes Jerusalem

key_moments.description: Nebuchadnezzar returned with all his army and besieged Jerusalem until the city ran out of food. In his nineteenth year his captain burned the LORD's house, and Jerusalem's walls were torn down.
key_moments.title: Has Jerusalem Burned

key_moments.description: Nebuchadnezzar dreamed of a great image of gold, silver, brass, iron and clay, broken by a stone that became a mountain. When Daniel told him the dream, the king fell on his face and said Daniel's God was God over all gods.
key_moments.title: Dreams of a Great Image

key_moments.description: Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image on the plain of Dura and commanded all to worship it. When three Jews refused, he threw them into a fiery furnace, then saw them walking unharmed and blessed their God.
key_moments.title: Sets Up a Golden Image

key_moments.description: As Nebuchadnezzar boasted over great Babylon, a voice spoke from heaven and took his kingdom away, and he ate grass like an ox. When his understanding came back, he praised and honored the King of heaven.
key_moments.title: Humbled, Then Praising God

name: Nebuchadnezzar
summary: A king of Babylon who took Jerusalem, carried its people away captive, and later had the city and the house of the LORD burned. In Babylon God humbled him, and he came to praise the King of heaven.

key_moments.description: When Naomi told her to go back to her own people, Ruth held on to her. She promised to go where Naomi went, to make Naomi's people her people and Naomi's God her God.
key_moments.title: Staying with Naomi

key_moments.description: Ruth gathered leftover grain in the field of Boaz, a relative of Naomi's husband. Boaz had heard of her kindness to Naomi, so he gave her food and told his young men to leave extra grain for her.
key_moments.title: Gleaning in Boaz's Field

key_moments.description: Ruth lay at the feet of Boaz in the night and asked him to spread his garment over her, because he was a near kinsman. He blessed her and said everyone knew she was a virtuous woman.
key_moments.title: Goes to Boaz at the Threshing Floor

key_moments.description: Boaz bought the land of Naomi's family and took Ruth as his wife before the elders. The LORD gave her a son, Obed, the grandfather of David.
key_moments.title: Marries Boaz

name: Ruth
summary: A woman of Moab who would not leave her mother-in-law Naomi and came to trust the God of Israel. She married Boaz of Bethlehem and became the great-grandmother of David.

key_moments.description: When some widows were being neglected in the daily sharing, the church chose seven trusted men, full of wisdom and the Holy Ghost, to look after it. Philip was one of them, and the apostles prayed and laid their hands on them.
key_moments.title: Chosen as One of the Seven

key_moments.description: Philip went down to Samaria and preached Christ, and the people listened as they saw the miracles he did. Many men and women believed and were baptized, even Simon the sorcerer.
key_moments.title: Preaching in Samaria

key_moments.description: An angel sent Philip to the desert road toward Gaza, where an Ethiopian official sat in his chariot reading the prophet Isaiah. Philip started from that scripture and preached Jesus to him, then baptized him, and the Spirit carried Philip away.
key_moments.title: Baptizes the Ethiopian

key_moments.description: When Paul and his company came to Caesarea, they stayed in the house of Philip the evangelist. Philip had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
key_moments.title: Hosts Paul in Caesarea

name: Philip
summary: One of the seven men chosen to serve the church, later called Philip the evangelist. He preached Christ in Samaria and baptized an Ethiopian official on a desert road.

key_moments.description: Pilate asked Jesus if He was the King of the Jews, and Jesus said His kingdom did not belong to this world. Pilate asked what truth is, then told the crowd he found no fault in Him.
key_moments.title: Finds No Fault in Jesus

key_moments.description: Pilate offered to release Jesus or Barabbas, and the crowd chose Barabbas and cried out for Jesus to be crucified. Pilate washed his hands before them, saying he was innocent of this just man's blood, and handed Jesus over.
key_moments.title: Washing His Hands

key_moments.description: Pilate had Jesus whipped, and soldiers put a crown of thorns and a purple robe on Him. Pilate brought Him out and tried to release Him, but the crowd cried out that Caesar was their only king, and he gave Jesus up to be crucified.
key_moments.title: Shows Jesus to the Crowd

key_moments.description: Pilate wrote a title for the cross: Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews. When the chief priests asked him to change it, he refused.
key_moments.title: Writes the Sign on the Cross

key_moments.description: Pilate gave the body of Jesus to Joseph of Arimathaea for burial. When the chief priests asked for the tomb to be guarded, Pilate told them to secure it as well as they could.
key_moments.title: Releases Jesus' Body to Joseph

name: Pontius Pilate
summary: The governor of Judaea who questioned Jesus and found no fault in Him. Pressed by the crowd, he released Barabbas and handed Jesus over to be crucified.

key_moments.description: Rabshakeh came from Lachish and stood at the upper pool's water channel. He asked what made Hezekiah so sure, scorned Egypt as a crushed reed, and even claimed the LORD had sent him to destroy the land.
key_moments.title: Mocks Hezekiah's Trust

key_moments.description: Hezekiah's men begged Rabshakeh to speak Syrian, not the Jews' language. Instead he shouted to the people on the wall, telling them Hezekiah could not save them, but they did not answer him a word.
key_moments.title: Shouting to the People

key_moments.description: Hezekiah hoped the LORD would rebuke Rabshakeh for mocking the living God, and Isaiah said not to fear his words. Rabshakeh went back to Assyria's king, who was fighting against Libnah.
key_moments.title: Returns to His King

name: Rabshakeh
summary: A man sent by Assyria's king with a huge army to Jerusalem. Standing outside the wall, he mocked King Hezekiah's faith in the LORD.

key_moments.description: Goliath of Gath, wearing armour of brass, came out from the Philistine camp in the valley of Elah. Each day for forty days he dared Israel to send a man against him, and Saul and all Israel were afraid.
key_moments.title: Defying the Armies of Israel

key_moments.description: Goliath mocked David and cursed him by his gods. David answered that he came in the LORD's name, then slung a stone into his forehead and cut off his head with his own sword.
key_moments.title: Struck Down by a Stone

name: Goliath
summary: A towering Philistine champion from Gath, who for forty days dared Israel to send a man to fight him. The young David killed him with a sling and a stone.

key_moments.description: Hananiah was among the young men of Judah taken into the king's court, and was given the name Shadrach. He and his friends ate vegetables and drank water instead of the king's food, and God gave them knowledge and wisdom.
key_moments.title: Renamed Shadrach in Babylon

key_moments.description: When the king's dream was a secret, Daniel asked Shadrach and his friends to pray to God for mercy. After Daniel told the dream, the king put the three in charge of Babylon's affairs.
key_moments.title: Set Over Babylon

key_moments.description: Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image and ordered everyone to worship it. Shadrach and his friends told the king their God was able to save them, but even if He did not, they would not bow.
key_moments.title: Refusing to Bow

key_moments.description: The three were tied up and thrown into a furnace heated seven times hotter. The king saw four men walking free in the fire, and they came out without even smelling of fire, so he praised their God and promoted them.
key_moments.title: Saved from the Fiery Furnace

name: Shadrach
summary: A young man of Judah, first called Hananiah, who was trained in the court of Babylon with Daniel. With Meshach and Abednego he refused to worship the king's golden image, and God brought them out of the furnace unharmed.

key_moments.description: The apostles and elders chose Silas and Judas, leading men among the believers, to take their letter to Antioch. Being prophets, they encouraged and strengthened the believers there with many words.
key_moments.title: Sent with the Letter

key_moments.description: After Paul and Barnabas parted, Paul chose Silas, and the believers sent them off, commending them to God's grace. They travelled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
key_moments.title: Chosen by Paul

key_moments.description: After Paul cast a spirit out of a fortune-telling girl, her masters had Paul and Silas beaten and thrown into prison. At midnight the two prayed and sang praises to God, and after an earthquake the jailer and his whole household believed.
key_moments.title: Sings in Prison at Midnight

key_moments.description: The believers sent Paul and Silas away by night to Berea, where many received the word eagerly. When trouble followed and Paul had to leave, Silas and Timotheus stayed on, and later they were told to join him at Athens.
key_moments.title: Sent Away to Berea

name: Silas
summary: A leader and prophet among the believers who carried the apostles' letter to Antioch. He became Paul's companion, sang with him in prison at midnight, and helped spread the word through Macedonia.

key_moments.description: Led by the Spirit, Simeon came into the temple when Jesus' parents brought Him there. He took the child in his arms, blessed God, and said he could now depart in peace, for he had seen God's salvation.
key_moments.title: Takes the Child Jesus in His Arms

key_moments.description: Simeon blessed Joseph and Mary and told Mary that this child would make many in Israel fall and rise again. He said a sword would pierce her own soul too.
key_moments.title: Warns Mary of a Sword

name: Simeon
summary: A just and devout man in Jerusalem who was waiting for the comfort of Israel. The Holy Ghost had shown him he would not die before seeing the Lord's Christ, and he took the baby Jesus in his arms in the temple.

key_moments.description: After Jesus prayed all night on a mountain, He called His disciples and chose twelve of them, whom He named apostles. Simon called Zelotes was one of the twelve.
key_moments.title: Chosen as One of the Twelve

key_moments.description: Jesus gave the twelve power to cast out unclean spirits and to heal every kind of sickness and disease, and sent them out. Simon the Canaanite is named among them.
key_moments.title: Sent Out to Preach and Heal

key_moments.description: After Jesus was taken up, the apostles went into an upper room in Jerusalem. Simon Zelotes was there, and they all kept on praying together with the women, Mary the mother of Jesus, and His brothers.
key_moments.title: Prays with the Others in the Upper Room

name: Simon
summary: One of the twelve apostles Jesus chose, called Simon Zelotes and Simon the Canaanite. Scripture names him in the lists of the twelve and among those praying in the upper room after Jesus was taken up.

key_moments.description: As Jesus was led away to be crucified, they seized Simon, a Cyrenian passing by on his way in from the country. They laid the cross on him and made him carry it behind Jesus.
key_moments.title: Carries Jesus' Cross

name: Simon
summary: A man of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, who was coming in from the country as Jesus was led away. The soldiers made him carry Jesus' cross.

key_moments.description: Simon had long amazed the people of Samaria with sorcery, and they said he was God's great power. When Philip preached, Simon believed too, was baptized, and stayed close to Philip, amazed at the miracles.
key_moments.title: Believes and Is Baptized

key_moments.description: When Simon saw the Holy Ghost given as the apostles laid on their hands, he offered them money for that power. Peter told him God's gift could not be bought with money and that he must repent, and Simon asked them to pray for him.
key_moments.title: Trying to Buy God's Gift

name: Simon
summary: A sorcerer in Samaria who had amazed the people, until he believed and was baptized when Philip preached. When he offered money for the power to give the Holy Ghost, Peter rebuked him.

key_moments.description: Tamar married Judah's son Er, who was wicked, and the LORD put him to death; his brother Onan died too. Judah sent her to live as a widow at her father's home until Shelah grew up.
key_moments.title: Loses Two Husbands

key_moments.description: Seeing that Shelah was grown but not given to her, Tamar veiled her face and sat by the road to Timnath. Judah thought she was a harlot, lay with her, and left his signet, bracelets and staff as a pledge.
key_moments.title: Disguises Herself by the Road

key_moments.description: When Judah heard she was with child, he ordered her burned, but she sent him his own pledge. Judah admitted she was more righteous than he, and she gave birth to twins, Pharez and Zarah.
key_moments.title: Saved by Judah's Pledge

name: Tamar
summary: The widow of Judah's son Er, left waiting when Judah did not give her to his son Shelah. She bore Judah twin sons, and he admitted she was more righteous than he.

key_moments.description: Ishbi-benob, one of the giant's sons, carried a heavy brass spear and meant to kill David, who had grown weary in battle. Abishai came to help David and killed the Philistine.
key_moments.title: His Son Threatens David

key_moments.description: Another son of the giant fell at Gob. At Gath a man of great size with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot defied Israel, and David's nephew Jonathan killed him.
key_moments.title: His Sons Fall to David's Men

name: the giant in Gath
summary: A giant of the Philistines whose four sons, born to him in Gath, fell by the hand of David and his servants. Scripture never shows the giant himself with anyone; it was his sons who fought.

key_moments.description: When Jesus decided to go back to Judaea, where people had tried to stone Him, Thomas told the other disciples they should go too, even to die with Him.
key_moments.title: Offers to Die with Jesus

key_moments.description: Thomas told Jesus they did not know where He was going or the way there. Jesus answered that He is the way, and no one comes to the Father except through Him.
key_moments.title: Asks Jesus the Way

key_moments.description: Thomas said he would not believe unless he saw the nail marks in Jesus' hands. Eight days later Jesus came, told him to look at His hands and touch His side, and Thomas called Him his Lord and his God.
key_moments.title: Believes After Seeing Jesus

name: Thomas
summary: One of the twelve apostles, also called Didymus. He would not believe Jesus had risen until he saw Him, and then he called Jesus his Lord and his God.

key_moments.description: Paul took Titus with him and Barnabas when he went up to Jerusalem. Though Titus was a Greek, he was not forced to be circumcised.
key_moments.title: Goes Up to Jerusalem with Paul

key_moments.description: When Paul came into Macedonia, troubled on all sides, God comforted him when Titus arrived. Titus brought news of the Corinthians' longing and care for Paul, which made him rejoice even more.
key_moments.title: Comforts Paul in Macedonia

key_moments.description: God gave Titus the same deep care for the Corinthians that Paul had, and he gladly went to them on his own. Paul called him his partner and fellow helper.
key_moments.title: Sent to the Corinthians

key_moments.description: Paul wrote to Titus as his own son in the faith they shared. He had left Titus in Crete to set right what was lacking and to appoint elders in each city.
key_moments.title: Left in Crete

name: Titus
summary: A Greek believer who travelled with Paul and was his trusted partner. Paul sent him to the Corinthians, was comforted by his coming, and left him in Crete to set things in order and appoint elders.

key_moments.description: Afraid of Israel's growing numbers, the new king set taskmasters over them, and they built the storage cities Pithom and Raamses for Pharaoh. Yet the harder they were treated, the more they grew.
key_moments.title: Puts Israel to Hard Labor

key_moments.description: He told the Hebrew midwives to kill every newborn son, but they feared God and let the boys live. Then Pharaoh commanded all his people to throw every newborn son into the river.
key_moments.title: Orders the Hebrew Boys Killed

key_moments.description: When Pharaoh heard that Moses had killed an Egyptian, he tried to kill Moses. Moses fled from him to Midian.
key_moments.title: Seeks to Kill Moses

name: Pharaoh
summary: The king of Egypt who did not know Joseph and feared how many the Israelites had become. He forced them into hard labor and ordered their newborn sons thrown into the river.

key_moments.description: The LORD said He would hand Pharaohhophra, king of Egypt, over to his enemies. It would be just as He had handed Zedekiah of Judah over to Nebuchadrezzar.
key_moments.title: Doomed to Fall to His Enemies

key_moments.description: The LORD told Ezekiel to prophesy against Pharaoh, the great dragon lying in his rivers, who said the river was his own and he had made it. The LORD would pull him out with hooks and leave him in the wilderness.
key_moments.title: Condemned as the Great Dragon

key_moments.description: The LORD said He had broken Pharaoh's arm, and it would not be healed to hold a sword. He would make the king of Babylon strong and give him His own sword to use against Egypt.
key_moments.title: His Arm Broken by the LORD

name: Pharaoh
summary: Pharaohhophra was a king of Egypt in the days of Jeremiah and Ezekiel. The LORD said He would hand him over to his enemies and break his arms before the king of Babylon.

key_moments.description: Ahaziah became king in Jerusalem after his father Jehoram. His mother Athaliah was Omri's daughter, and with her and Ahab's house as his counsellors, he did evil like the house of Ahab.
key_moments.title: Follows the Ways of Ahab's House

key_moments.description: Ahaziah went with Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead. When Joram was wounded, Ahaziah went down to Jezreel to see him.
key_moments.title: Fights Syria Beside Joram

key_moments.description: Ahaziah rode out with Joram to meet Jehu. When Jehu shot Joram, Ahaziah fled, and Jehu's men struck him in his chariot near Ibleam. He fled to Megiddo and died there, and was buried in Jerusalem.
key_moments.title: Struck Down Fleeing from Jehu

name: Ahaziah
summary: The youngest son of Jehoram king of Judah, who reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother Athaliah counselled him to follow Ahab's house, and Jehu struck him down when he went to visit King Joram.

key_moments.description: Saul's daughter Michal loved David, and Saul gave her to him as wife, hoping the Philistines would kill David. David brought the price Saul asked, and Saul saw that the LORD was with him.
key_moments.title: Given to David as His Wife

key_moments.description: When Saul sent men to kill David, Michal let him down through a window. She put an image in his bed with goats' hair at its head to fool the messengers.
key_moments.title: Helps David Escape Through a Window

key_moments.description: Saul gave Michal to another man, Phalti of Gallim. Later David demanded her back, and her husband followed her weeping until Abner sent him home.
key_moments.title: Given Away and Taken Back

key_moments.description: Michal watched from a window as David leaped and danced before the LORD, and she despised him. She mocked him, and she had no child to the day of her death.
key_moments.title: Mocks David for Dancing

name: Michal
summary: A daughter of King Saul who loved David, became his wife, and once saved his life from her father. Later she despised David for dancing before the LORD, and she had no child to the day of her death.

key_moments.description: Jonathan and his armourbearer climbed up to a Philistine post alone, saying the LORD could save with many or with few. They struck down about twenty men, and the whole Philistine army trembled.
key_moments.title: Climbing to the Philistine Camp

key_moments.description: Not knowing his father had forbidden the army to eat that day, Jonathan tasted some honey. Saul would have put him to death, but the people rescued Jonathan.
key_moments.title: Eats Honey Against Saul's Oath

key_moments.description: Jonathan loved David as much as himself and made a covenant with him. He gave David his robe, his sword, his bow and his belt.
key_moments.title: Makes a Covenant with David

key_moments.description: Jonathan shot arrows past a boy as a sign to warn David that Saul meant to kill him. The two friends kissed and wept, and Jonathan sent David away in peace.
key_moments.title: Warns David with Arrows

key_moments.description: The Philistines killed Jonathan with his father on Mount Gilboa. David mourned him in a song and said Jonathan had been very dear to him.
key_moments.title: Fallen at Gilboa

name: Jonathan
summary: A son of King Saul and a bold warrior, who made a covenant of friendship with David and protected him from his father. He died beside Saul in battle on Mount Gilboa.

key_moments.description: Eve bore another son and named him Seth, saying God had given her another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain killed. Adam was a hundred and thirty years old, and Seth was born in his likeness, after his image.
key_moments.title: Born in Abel's Place

key_moments.description: When Seth was a hundred and five years old, a son was born to him, and he called him Enos. Then men began to call on the name of the LORD.
key_moments.title: Names His Son Enos

key_moments.description: After Enos was born, Seth lived eight hundred and seven more years and had sons and daughters. All his days were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.
key_moments.title: Dies at 912 Years Old

name: Seth
summary: The son born to Adam and Eve after Cain killed Abel. After his son Enos was born, men began to call on the name of the LORD.

key_moments.description: Hezekiah did right like David his father. He took away the high places and smashed the bronze serpent Moses had made, because Israel had been burning incense to it.
key_moments.title: Breaking the Bronze Serpent

key_moments.description: Hezekiah took the king of Assyria's threatening letter into the LORD's house and spread it out before Him in prayer. That night the angel of the LORD struck the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib went home to Nineveh.
key_moments.title: Spreads Assyria's Letter Before the LORD

key_moments.description: When Hezekiah was dying, he prayed and wept, and the LORD promised to heal him and add fifteen years to his life. As a sign, the shadow went back ten steps on the dial of Ahaz.
key_moments.title: Given Fifteen More Years

key_moments.description: Hezekiah showed the messengers from Babylon everything in his storehouses. Isaiah then told him that all of it would one day be carried off to Babylon.
key_moments.title: Shows His Treasures to Babylon

key_moments.description: Hezekiah sent letters across Israel and Judah, calling people to Jerusalem to celebrate the passover. He prayed for those who were not clean, and the LORD heard him, and Jerusalem had its greatest joy since Solomon.
key_moments.title: Holds a Great Passover

name: Hezekiah
summary: A son of Ahaz who became king of Judah and trusted the LORD like no other king of Judah. When Assyria threatened Jerusalem, he prayed, and the LORD saved the city.

key_moments.description: In Derbe and Lystra Paul found a disciple named Timotheus, whose mother was a Jewish believer and whose father was a Greek. The believers spoke well of him, and Paul took him along on his travels.
key_moments.title: Joining Paul

key_moments.description: While Paul waited alone at Athens, he sent Timotheus to strengthen and comfort the Thessalonian believers in their troubles. Timotheus came back with good news of their faith and love.
key_moments.title: Sent to Thessalonica

name: Timotheus
summary: A disciple with a believing Jewish mother and a Greek father, who became Paul's close helper on his travels. Paul sent him to strengthen the churches and called him his dearly beloved son.

key_moments.description: Caleb quieted the people in front of Moses and told them to go up at once, for they could surely win. With Joshua, he urged them not to rebel against the LORD or fear the people living there.
key_moments.title: Urges Israel to Take the Land

key_moments.description: The LORD said Caleb had another spirit in him and had followed Him fully. So Caleb would enter the land, and his children would possess it.
key_moments.title: Promised He Will Enter the Land

key_moments.description: At eighty-five, Caleb told Joshua he was as strong as when Moses sent him to spy, and asked for the hill country the LORD had promised. Joshua blessed him and gave him Hebron.
key_moments.title: Asks for Hebron at Eighty-Five

key_moments.description: Caleb drove Anak's three sons out of Hebron and promised his daughter Achsah to whoever took Kirjathsepher. Othniel took it and married her, and Caleb gave her the upper and lower springs she asked for.
key_moments.title: Gives Achsah the Springs

name: Caleb
summary: A spy from the tribe of Judah who trusted the LORD when others were afraid. Because he followed the LORD with his whole heart, he lived to receive Hebron as his inheritance.

key_moments.description: Manasseh rebuilt the high places his father had torn down, set up altars to Baal, and built altars inside the LORD's house. He even put his son through the fire and dealt with spirits and wizards.
key_moments.title: Undoing His Father's Work

key_moments.description: The LORD said through His prophets that He would bring great trouble on Jerusalem for what Manasseh had done. Manasseh also shed so much innocent blood that it filled Jerusalem from end to end.
key_moments.title: Fills Jerusalem with Innocent Blood

key_moments.description: The LORD let the king of Assyria's captains bind Manasseh in chains and carry him to Babylon. There he humbled himself and prayed, and the LORD brought him back to Jerusalem, and Manasseh came to know the LORD is God.
key_moments.title: Humbled in Babylon

key_moments.description: Back in Jerusalem, Manasseh removed the idol and the foreign gods from the LORD's house and threw out his altars. He repaired the LORD's altar and commanded Judah to worship the LORD, Israel's God.
key_moments.title: Clearing Out the Idols

name: Manasseh
summary: A son of Hezekiah who became king of Judah at twelve and led the people into more evil than the nations before them. Taken in chains to Babylon, he humbled himself, and the LORD brought him home.

key_moments.description: Ahaziah became king of Israel, ruling from Samaria. He did evil, following his father and mother, and he served and worshipped Baal.
key_moments.title: Serves Baal Like His Father

key_moments.description: Ahaziah fell through a window lattice upstairs and sent messengers to ask Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, if he would get well. Elijah met them with the LORD's word that he would never leave his bed, and he died.
key_moments.title: Asks Baal-zebub If He Will Recover

key_moments.description: Jehoshaphat king of Judah teamed up with Ahaziah to build ships bound for Tarshish. A prophet said the LORD would break them for this, and the ships were wrecked.
key_moments.title: Builds Ships with Jehoshaphat

name: Ahaziah
summary: A son of Ahab who ruled Israel from Samaria for two years and served Baal as his father had. After a fall he sent to ask a foreign god whether he would recover, and he died as Elijah said.

key_moments.description: Miriam took a timbrel, and all the women followed her with timbrels and dancing. She sang that the LORD had thrown horse and rider into the sea.
key_moments.title: Leads the Women in Song

key_moments.description: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses, and the LORD rebuked them at the tabernacle. Miriam became leprous, and after Moses prayed for her, she was kept outside the camp for seven days.
key_moments.title: Struck with Leprosy

key_moments.description: Israel reached the desert of Zin and stayed at Kadesh. There Miriam died and was buried.
key_moments.title: Dies at Kadesh

name: Miriam
summary: A prophetess and the sister of Aaron and Moses, who led the women in song after the LORD's victory at the sea. She died at Kadesh in the desert of Zin.

key_moments.description: While Israel lived beyond the tower of Edar, Reuben lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine, and Israel heard about it.
key_moments.title: Lies with His Father's Concubine

key_moments.description: When his brothers plotted to kill Joseph, Reuben talked them into throwing him into a pit instead, planning to bring him back to their father. When Reuben returned and found the pit empty, he tore his clothes.
key_moments.title: Trying to Save Joseph

key_moments.description: In Egypt, Reuben reminded his brothers that he had warned them not to harm Joseph. Back home, he offered his own two sons to Jacob as a pledge that he would bring Benjamin back.
key_moments.title: Pledging His Sons

key_moments.description: Jacob called Reuben his firstborn and the beginning of his strength. But he said Reuben was unstable as water and would not excel, because he had gone up to his father's bed.
key_moments.title: Rebuked in Jacob's Last Words

name: Reuben
summary: Jacob's firstborn son, born to Leah. He tried to save Joseph when the brothers planned to kill him, but Jacob said he would not excel because he had defiled his father's bed.

key_moments.description: Jesus saw James and John in their boat mending their nets and called them. They left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired servants and followed Jesus.
key_moments.title: Leaving the Nets

key_moments.description: Jesus took Peter, John and James up a mountain to pray. As He prayed His face changed and His clothes shone, and Moses and Elijah talked with Him.
key_moments.title: Sees Jesus Changed on the Mountain

key_moments.description: Peter and John met a man lame from birth at the temple gate called Beautiful. Peter healed him in Jesus' name, and the man held on to them as the people ran together in wonder.
key_moments.title: Sees a Lame Man Healed at the Gate

key_moments.description: The rulers marvelled at the boldness of Peter and John, though they were unlearned men. Told to stop speaking about Jesus, they answered that they could not stop telling what they had seen and heard.
key_moments.title: Refuses to Stop Speaking of Jesus

name: John
summary: A fisherman, the son of Zebedee and brother of James, who became one of the twelve apostles. After Jesus rose, he and Peter healed a lame man and spoke boldly before the council.

key_moments.description: When the army of Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem, Jehoiachin gave himself up to the king of Babylon with his mother, servants and princes. He was taken to Babylon, along with the LORD's temple treasures and thousands of captives.
key_moments.title: Carried Away to Babylon

key_moments.description: In the thirty-seventh year of his captivity, Evilmerodach king of Babylon brought Jehoiachin out of prison. He spoke kindly to him, gave him a seat higher than the other kings there, and fed him at his table for the rest of his life.
key_moments.title: Brought Out of Prison

key_moments.description: The LORD said that even if Coniah were the signet ring on His right hand, He would pull him off. He would give him to Nebuchadrezzar and cast him out into a land he did not know.
key_moments.title: Cast Off Like a Signet Ring

name: Jehoiachin
summary: A son of Jehoiakim who reigned over Judah for only three months before he was carried away captive to Babylon. After many years in prison there, a new king of Babylon set him free and gave him a place at his table.

key_moments.description: At Shechem the people asked Rehoboam to lighten the heavy yoke his father had put on them. He turned from the counsel of the old men, followed the young men, and promised them a heavier yoke.
key_moments.title: Answers the People Harshly

key_moments.description: Israel rejected the house of David and stoned Adoram, the officer over the tribute. Rehoboam fled to Jerusalem in his chariot, and only Judah followed the house of David.
key_moments.title: Loses the Northern Tribes

key_moments.description: Rehoboam gathered an army to win back the kingdom, but the LORD sent word by Shemaiah not to fight against their brothers. The people listened and went home.
key_moments.title: Told Not to Fight

key_moments.description: Shishak king of Egypt came against Jerusalem and took away the treasures, including the shields of gold Solomon had made. Rehoboam made shields of brass in their place.
key_moments.title: Replaces the Gold Shields with Brass

name: Rehoboam
summary: The son of Solomon who became king after him. When he answered the people harshly, the tribes of Israel broke away, and he was left to reign over Judah from Jerusalem.

key_moments.description: Pharaohnechoh made Eliakim son of Josiah king and changed his name to Jehoiakim. Jehoiakim taxed the people of the land to pay the silver and gold Pharaoh demanded, and he did evil in the LORD's eyes.
key_moments.title: Made King by Pharaoh

key_moments.description: When Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, Jehoiakim served him for three years, then turned against him. The LORD sent bands of raiders against Judah, as His prophets had said.
key_moments.title: Rebelling Against Babylon

key_moments.description: When the prophet Urijah spoke against the city as Jeremiah did, Jehoiakim tried to kill him. Urijah fled to Egypt, but the king had him brought back and put him to death by the sword.
key_moments.title: Has the Prophet Urijah Killed

key_moments.description: As Jehudi read Jeremiah's scroll to the king by the fire, a few leaves at a time were cut off and thrown into the flames until the king had burned it all. The LORD said none of Jehoiakim's line would sit on David's throne.
key_moments.title: Burns Jeremiah's Scroll

name: Jehoiakim
summary: A son of King Josiah whom the king of Egypt set on the throne of Judah, changing his name from Eliakim. He did evil in the LORD's eyes and burned the scroll of the LORD's words that had been written down as Jeremiah spoke them.

key_moments.description: Joab's men and Abner's men met at the pool of Gibeon, and a fierce battle followed. Abner's men lost, and Joab's brother Asahel was killed chasing Abner.
key_moments.title: Fights Abner at the Pool of Gibeon

key_moments.description: When Joab heard David had sent Abner away in peace, he called Abner back to Hebron. He took him aside in the gate and killed him for the blood of his brother Asahel.
key_moments.title: Killing Abner

key_moments.description: David wrote to Joab to put Uriah in the front of the fiercest fighting. Joab set Uriah where the strongest enemy men were, and Uriah was killed.
key_moments.title: Puts Uriah Where the Fighting Is Fiercest

key_moments.description: The king told his captains to deal gently with Absalom. But when Absalom hung caught in an oak, Joab thrust three darts into his heart.
key_moments.title: Strikes Down Absalom Against David's Order

key_moments.description: Joab had followed Adonijah, and when he heard the news he fled and caught hold of the altar. Solomon sent Benaiah, who killed him there for the innocent blood he had shed.
key_moments.title: Killed While Holding the Altar

name: Joab
summary: A son of Zeruiah and the captain of David's army, who led many of David's battles. He killed Abner, Absalom and Amasa with his own hand, and in Solomon's day he was put to death at the altar.

key_moments.description: Zilpah, Leah's maid, bore Jacob a second son. Leah said she was happy, for the daughters would call her blessed, and named him Asher.
key_moments.title: Born to Zilpah

key_moments.description: Asher went down to Egypt with his father Jacob and the whole family, along with his sons.
key_moments.title: Goes Down to Egypt

key_moments.description: Jacob said that out of Asher his bread would be fat, and he would yield royal dainties.
key_moments.title: Blessed by Jacob

name: Asher
summary: A son of Jacob, born to Zilpah, Leah's maid. Jacob said Asher's bread would be rich and he would give food fit for kings.

key_moments.description: In the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah saw the Lord on a high throne, with seraphims calling Him holy. A live coal touched his lips to take away his sin, and when the Lord asked who would go, Isaiah offered himself.
key_moments.title: Sees the Lord on His Throne

key_moments.description: When Syria and Israel threatened Judah, the LORD sent Isaiah to meet King Ahaz and tell him not to fear their plans. Isaiah then gave the sign of a virgin who would bear a son named Immanuel.
key_moments.title: Gives Ahaz the Sign of Immanuel

key_moments.description: The LORD told Isaiah to take off his sackcloth and shoes. He went about naked and barefoot for three years, as a sign of how Assyria would lead away the people of Egypt and Ethiopia.
key_moments.title: Walks Barefoot for Three Years as a Sign

key_moments.description: When Assyria mocked the LORD, King Hezekiah's servants came to Isaiah. He told them the LORD said not to fear, for the king of Assyria would hear a rumor and go home.
key_moments.title: Tells Hezekiah Not to Fear Assyria

key_moments.description: Isaiah told the dying Hezekiah to set his house in order, but after the king prayed, the LORD sent Isaiah back to promise fifteen more years. As a sign, the shadow on the dial of Ahaz went back ten steps.
key_moments.title: Promises Hezekiah Fifteen More Years

name: Isaiah
summary: A prophet, the son of Amoz, who saw visions about Judah and Jerusalem during the reigns of four kings, from Uzziah to Hezekiah. He brought the LORD's word to kings in times of war and sickness.

key_moments.description: The LORD told Jonah to go and cry against Nineveh for its wickedness. Instead Jonah fled to Joppa and paid for a ship heading the other way, to Tarshish.
key_moments.title: Running from the LORD

key_moments.description: The LORD sent a great storm, and the lot showed the sailors that Jonah was the cause. At his word they threw him overboard, the sea grew calm, and a great fish swallowed him for three days and nights.
key_moments.title: Thrown into the Sea

key_moments.description: From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the LORD his God and thanked Him for hearing him. Then the LORD spoke to the fish, and it threw Jonah up onto dry land.
key_moments.title: Prays from Inside the Fish

key_moments.description: Jonah walked into Nineveh crying that in forty days the city would be overthrown. The people believed God, fasted and turned from their wicked ways, and God did not destroy them.
key_moments.title: Warns Nineveh, and the City Turns

key_moments.description: Jonah was angry that God spared Nineveh. God grew a gourd to shade him and then sent a worm to kill it, and asked whether He should not spare that great city with all its people.
key_moments.title: Angry When God Spares Nineveh

name: Jonah
summary: A prophet, the son of Amittai, whom the LORD sent to warn the great city of Nineveh. He ran from the LORD, was swallowed by a great fish, and was angry when God spared the city.

key_moments.description: After Jesus prayed all night on a mountain, He called His disciples and chose twelve of them, whom He named apostles. Thaddaeus, named here as Judas the brother of James, was one of the twelve.
key_moments.title: Chosen as One of the Twelve

key_moments.description: Jesus gave the twelve power to cast out unclean spirits and to heal every kind of sickness and disease, and sent them out. Thaddaeus, called here Lebbaeus whose surname was Thaddaeus, is named among them.
key_moments.title: Sent Out to Preach and Heal

key_moments.description: Judas, not Judas Iscariot, asked Jesus how He would show Himself to the disciples and not to the world. Jesus answered that if a man loves Him, he will keep His words, and the Father and He will come and make their home with him.
key_moments.title: Asks Jesus Why He Shows Himself Only to Them

name: Thaddaeus
summary: One of the twelve apostles, also called Lebbaeus and Judas the brother of James. He is not Judas Iscariot, the one who betrayed Jesus.

key_moments.description: Darius took the kingdom at about sixty-two years old. He set 120 princes over it, with three presidents above them, and Daniel was first among them.
key_moments.title: Taking the Kingdom

key_moments.description: Leaders who could find no fault in Daniel asked Darius to sign a law that for thirty days no one could pray to any god or man but the king. Darius signed it, and it could not be changed.
key_moments.title: Signing the Decree

key_moments.description: Darius tried until sunset to save Daniel but had to let him be thrown to the lions. He fasted and could not sleep, then hurried to the den at dawn and found Daniel alive.
key_moments.title: Spends a Sleepless Night for Daniel

key_moments.description: King Darius wrote to all people that they must tremble and fear before Daniel's God, the living God who had saved Daniel from the lions.
key_moments.title: Decrees That All Fear Daniel's God

name: Darius
summary: Darius the Median took the kingdom after Belshazzar and made Daniel one of his top leaders. Talked into a law that sent Daniel to the lions, he saw God rescue Daniel and told all nations to fear Daniel's God.

key_moments.description: Asa removed the idols his fathers had made. He even removed his mother Maachah from being queen because of her idol, and burned it by the brook Kidron.
key_moments.title: Cleansing the Land

key_moments.description: Zerah the Ethiopian came against Judah with a huge army near Mareshah. Asa cried to the LORD for help, and the LORD struck the Ethiopians before Judah.
key_moments.title: Cries to the LORD Before Battle

key_moments.description: After the prophet Azariah urged him on, Asa put away the idols and gathered the people at Jerusalem. They swore together with shouting and trumpets that they would seek the LORD with their whole heart.
key_moments.title: Leads Judah to Seek the LORD

key_moments.description: When Baasha king of Israel built Ramah against Judah, Asa sent silver and gold to Ben-hadad of Syria for help. The seer Hanani rebuked him for relying on Syria and not the LORD, and Asa put him in prison.
key_moments.title: Paying Syria for Help

key_moments.description: In his last years Asa was diseased in his feet, yet he did not seek the LORD, only the physicians. He died and was buried in the tomb he had made in the city of David.
key_moments.title: Seeks Physicians, Not the LORD

name: Asa
summary: A king of Judah, son of Abijah, who did what was right in the eyes of the LORD and put away the idols in the land. Later he relied on the king of Syria instead of the LORD, and in his disease he sought the physicians.

key_moments.description: When the kings of Syria and Israel came against Jerusalem, Ahaz begged Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria to save him. He sent him silver and gold from the LORD's house, and Assyria attacked Damascus.
key_moments.title: Begs Assyria for Help

key_moments.description: Visiting the king of Assyria at Damascus, Ahaz saw an altar there and sent its pattern home. Urijah the priest built a copy, and Ahaz moved the LORD's bronze altar off to one side.
key_moments.title: Copies an Altar from Damascus

key_moments.description: In his distress Ahaz sinned even more, offering sacrifices to the gods of Damascus. He cut up the vessels of God's house, shut its doors, and set up altars all over Jerusalem.
key_moments.title: Shuts the Doors of God's House

key_moments.description: The LORD told Ahaz to ask for a sign, but Ahaz refused to ask. So the Lord Himself would give a sign: a virgin would have a son, named Immanuel.
key_moments.title: Refuses to Ask for a Sign

name: Ahaz
summary: A son of Jotham who ruled Judah for sixteen years and did not do what was right as David had. In his troubles he turned to Assyria's king and to foreign gods, and he shut up the LORD's house.

key_moments.description: Jezebel cut off the prophets of the LORD. But Obadiah hid a hundred of them in caves and fed them with bread and water.
key_moments.title: Killing the Prophets

key_moments.description: When Ahab told her that Elijah had killed the prophets of Baal, Jezebel sent a messenger swearing to take Elijah's life by the next day. Elijah fled for his life.
key_moments.title: Threatens Elijah's Life

key_moments.description: Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab's name telling the elders to have false witnesses accuse Naboth. Naboth was stoned, and Jezebel told Ahab to go and take the vineyard.
key_moments.title: Has Naboth Stoned for His Vineyard

key_moments.description: When Jehu came to Jezreel, Jezebel painted her face and looked out a window. At Jehu's word she was thrown down and killed, just as the LORD had said through Elijah.
key_moments.title: Thrown from the Window

name: Jezebel
summary: The daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians and wife of King Ahab. She killed the prophets of the LORD, threatened Elijah, and had Naboth stoned for his vineyard.

key_moments.description: Zephaniah said the LORD would stretch out His hand on Judah and Jerusalem and cut off those who worshipped Baal and the host of heaven. The great day of the LORD was near, a day of wrath, and silver and gold would not save them.
key_moments.title: Warns the Day of the LORD Is Near

key_moments.description: Zephaniah called the nation to gather before the LORD's fierce anger came. He told the meek of the earth to seek the LORD, righteousness and meekness, so they might be hidden in the day of His anger.
key_moments.title: Tells the Meek to Seek the LORD

key_moments.description: Zephaniah told Zion to sing and Jerusalem to rejoice, for the LORD had cast out her enemy. The LORD in her midst would save, rejoice over her with singing, and gather His scattered people home.
key_moments.title: Says the LORD Will Rejoice Over Zion

name: Zephaniah
summary: A prophet, the son of Cushi, who warned in the days of King Josiah that the day of the LORD was near and told the meek to seek the LORD. Scripture tells nothing more about him, and no story places him with anyone else.

key_moments.description: Living with the captives at the river Chebar, Ezekiel saw the heavens open and was shown visions from God. Out of a whirlwind of cloud and fire came four living creatures that looked like men.
key_moments.title: Sees Visions by the River Chebar

key_moments.description: The LORD told Ezekiel that the delight of his eyes would be taken, yet he must not mourn or weep. That evening his wife died, and he did as he was told, so that he became a sign to the people.
key_moments.title: Forbidden to Mourn His Wife

key_moments.description: The LORD set Ezekiel in a valley full of dry bones and told him to prophesy to them. The bones joined, flesh covered them, and breath entered them, and they stood up, a very great army.
key_moments.title: Prophesies to Dry Bones

name: Ezekiel
summary: Ezekiel son of Buzi was a priest living with the captives at the river Chebar, in the land of the Chaldeans. There the LORD gave him visions and words to speak to His people, and even made his own life a sign to them.

key_moments.description: When Mary was found to be with child by the Holy Ghost, Joseph planned to end the engagement quietly. An angel told him in a dream not to fear, so he took Mary as his wife and named the baby Jesus.
key_moments.title: Told in a Dream to Take Mary

key_moments.description: Joseph went from Nazareth to Bethlehem, David's city, to be taxed with Mary. There she gave birth to Jesus and placed Him in a manger.
key_moments.title: Travels to Bethlehem with Mary

key_moments.description: An angel warned Joseph in a dream that Herod would seek the child to kill Him. Joseph took the child and His mother by night and fled to Egypt.
key_moments.title: Flees to Egypt with the Child

key_moments.description: After Herod died, an angel told Joseph to go back to Israel. Warned again in a dream, he settled in Galilee, in the town of Nazareth.
key_moments.title: Settles in Nazareth

key_moments.description: When Jesus was twelve, He stayed behind in Jerusalem after the feast without Joseph and Mary knowing. After three days of searching they found Him in the temple with the teachers.
key_moments.title: Searching for Jesus

name: Joseph
summary: A just man of the house of David who was engaged to Mary, the mother of Jesus. Guided by an angel in dreams, he took Mary as his wife and kept the young child safe.

key_moments.description: The king's prophets all said to go up to Ramoth-gilead and win. When Micaiah was sent for, he was told to agree with them, but he promised to speak only what the LORD told him.
key_moments.title: Vows to Speak Only the LORD's Word

key_moments.description: Micaiah saw Israel scattered over the hills like sheep with no shepherd. He told of seeing the LORD on His throne, and said a lying spirit was speaking through the king's prophets.
key_moments.title: Warns Ahab He Will Fall

key_moments.description: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah slapped Micaiah's face, and the king had him jailed on scant bread and water. Micaiah answered that if the king ever came home safely, the LORD had not spoken through him.
key_moments.title: Struck and Sent to Prison

name: Micaiah
summary: A prophet, the son of Imlah, whom Israel's king hated, saying he only ever foretold trouble for him. When four hundred prophets promised victory at Ramoth-gilead, Micaiah alone spoke the LORD's warning.

key_moments.description: Hiram sent messengers to David with cedar trees, carpenters and masons. They built David a house.
key_moments.title: Sends Builders to David

key_moments.description: When Solomon asked for help building a house for the LORD, Hiram rejoiced and blessed the LORD. He sent cedar and fir trees, Solomon paid him in wheat and oil, and the two kings made a league of peace.
key_moments.title: Sends Cedar for the Temple

key_moments.description: Hiram sent his own sailors, men who knew the sea, with Solomon's servants. They sailed to Ophir and brought back gold for King Solomon.
key_moments.title: Sends His Sailors to Ophir

name: Hiram
