summary: The king of Tyre and a friend to both David and Solomon. He sent cedar wood and skilled workers for their building, and his ships brought gold from Ophir.

key_moments.description: The LORD told Jeremiah He had known him and set him apart as a prophet before he was born. When Jeremiah said he was only a child, the LORD touched his mouth and put His words there.
key_moments.title: Called as a Child

key_moments.description: The LORD sent Jeremiah to watch a potter remake a spoiled clay pot into another. He said Israel was in His hands just as clay is held by a potter.
key_moments.title: Sent to the Potter's House

key_moments.description: While Jeremiah was shut in the prison court, he bought his cousin's field in Anathoth and sealed the deed before witnesses. The LORD said that houses, fields and vineyards would one day be owned in the land again.
key_moments.title: Buying a Field

key_moments.description: The princes lowered Jeremiah on cords into a dungeon with no water, and he sank in the mud. Ebedmelech the Ethiopian asked the king for help, and with thirty men he drew Jeremiah up with ropes and old rags.
key_moments.title: Lowered into a Dungeon

key_moments.description: After Jeremiah told the people the LORD's word not to go to Egypt, the leaders said he was lying. They took all who were left, Jeremiah and Baruch too, and went to Tahpanhes in Egypt.
key_moments.title: Taken to Egypt

name: Jeremiah
summary: A prophet from a priestly family in Anathoth whom the LORD called while he was young to speak His words to Judah and the nations. He warned of the fall of Jerusalem for many years and was beaten, imprisoned and thrown into a dungeon for it.

key_moments.description: Eliakim went out with Shebna and Joah to meet Rabshakeh and asked him to use Syrian, not the Jews' language, where the people on the wall could hear. Then, with torn clothes, they reported his words to Hezekiah.
key_moments.title: Speaks with Rabshakeh at the Wall

key_moments.description: Hezekiah sent Eliakim, Shebna and the senior priests, all in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah. Isaiah sent back word from the LORD not to be afraid.
key_moments.title: Sent to Isaiah

key_moments.description: The LORD called Eliakim His servant and said He would put the government into his hands. He would be like a father to Jerusalem and Judah, with the key of David's house laid on his shoulder.
key_moments.title: Promised the Key of David's House

name: Eliakim
summary: The son of Hilkiah, who was over King Hezekiah's household. He spoke for the king when Rabshakeh came from Assyria to Jerusalem's wall.

key_moments.description: On the way to Timnath a young lion roared at Samson, and the Spirit of the LORD came on him, so he tore it apart with his bare hands. Later he found bees and honey in its body.
key_moments.title: Tearing Apart a Lion

key_moments.description: The men of Judah bound Samson and handed him to the Philistines at Lehi. The Spirit of the LORD came on him, the ropes fell off, and he killed a thousand men with the jawbone of a donkey.
key_moments.title: Kills a Thousand Men with a Jawbone

key_moments.description: When the men of Gaza waited to kill him, Samson rose at midnight, pulled up the city gates, posts and all, and carried them to the top of a hill before Hebron.
key_moments.title: Carrying Off the Gates of Gaza

key_moments.description: After Delilah pressed him day after day, Samson told her no razor had ever touched his head. She had his hair shaved while he slept, the LORD left him, and the Philistines took him.
key_moments.title: Delilah Learns His Secret

key_moments.description: Blinded and made to grind in prison at Gaza, Samson was brought out to entertain the Philistines at a feast for their god Dagon. He prayed for strength one last time and leaned on the two middle pillars, and the house fell, killing more at his death than in his life.
key_moments.title: Bringing Down the House

name: Samson
summary: A Nazarite from birth, given great strength by the Spirit of the LORD, who judged Israel twenty years in the days of the Philistines. Betrayed by Delilah and blinded, he pulled down the house of Dagon on the Philistines at his death.

key_moments.description: Rachel came to a well near Haran with her father's sheep. Jacob rolled the stone from the well, watered her flock, kissed her and wept.
key_moments.title: Meeting at the Well

key_moments.description: Jacob loved Rachel and served seven years for her, and they seemed like only a few days to him. Laban gave him Leah first, and Jacob served seven more years for Rachel.
key_moments.title: Married to Jacob After Leah

key_moments.description: Rachel had no children and envied her sister. Then God remembered Rachel, and she bore a son and named him Joseph.
key_moments.title: Gives Birth to Joseph

key_moments.description: When Jacob's family left, Rachel stole her father's household idols. She hid them in the camel's saddle and sat on them while Laban searched the tent.
key_moments.title: Hiding Her Father's Idols

key_moments.description: On the way to Ephrath, Rachel died giving birth to her second son. She named him Benoni, Jacob called him Benjamin, and Jacob set up a pillar on her grave.
key_moments.title: Dies Giving Birth to Benjamin

name: Rachel
summary: Laban's younger daughter, whom Jacob loved and worked fourteen years for. She was the mother of Joseph and Benjamin, and she died giving birth to Benjamin.

key_moments.description: While searching for his father's lost donkeys, Saul came to Samuel, whom the LORD had told to expect him. Samuel poured oil on Saul's head and anointed him captain over the LORD's people.
key_moments.title: Anointed While Seeking Donkeys

key_moments.description: Saul spared King Agag and the best of the animals of Amalek, though the LORD had said to destroy them. Samuel told him that obeying the LORD matters more than sacrifice, and that the LORD had rejected him as king.
key_moments.title: Rejected for Disobeying

key_moments.description: The women sang that Saul had slain thousands but David ten thousands, and from that day Saul eyed David. An evil spirit came on Saul, and he threw a javelin at David twice.
key_moments.title: Throws a Javelin at David

key_moments.description: With the Philistines against him and no answer from God, Saul went in disguise to a woman with a familiar spirit at En-dor. Samuel appeared and told him he and his sons would die the next day.
key_moments.title: Consults the Woman at En-dor

key_moments.description: The Philistines killed his sons on Mount Gilboa, and archers badly wounded Saul. When his armourbearer would not kill him, Saul fell on his own sword.
key_moments.title: Falls on His Own Sword

name: Saul
summary: A tall young man of the tribe of Benjamin, the king the LORD gave Israel when they asked for one. He disobeyed the LORD, grew jealous of David, and died in battle on Mount Gilboa.

key_moments.description: Caleb promised his daughter Achsah as wife to the man who took Kirjath-sepher. Othniel took it, and Caleb gave him Achsah.
key_moments.title: Takes Kirjath-sepher and Wins Achsah

key_moments.description: Israel forgot the LORD and served Baalim, so the LORD sold them to Chushan-rishathaim, king of Mesopotamia, for eight years. When they cried to the LORD, He raised up Othniel to deliver them.
key_moments.title: Raised Up to Deliver Israel

key_moments.description: The Spirit of the LORD came upon Othniel, and he judged Israel and went out to war. The LORD gave Chushan-rishathaim into his hand, and the land had rest forty years.
key_moments.title: Defeats the King of Mesopotamia

name: Othniel
summary: The son of Kenaz and younger brother of Caleb, who took a city to win Caleb's daughter Achsah. When Israel cried out after eight years under the king of Mesopotamia, the LORD raised him up as a deliverer, and the land had rest forty years.

key_moments.description: When the people gathered in Jerusalem, Jeshua and the priests, with Zerubbabel, built an altar to Israel's God. Burnt offerings were made on it every morning and evening, as Moses' law said.
key_moments.title: Rebuilds the Altar of God

key_moments.description: The LORD sent word through Haggai to Zerubbabel, Joshua the high priest and all the people. He told them to be strong and work, for He was with them.
key_moments.title: Told to Be Strong and Work

key_moments.description: In a vision, Joshua stood in front of the angel of the LORD in filthy clothes, with Satan beside him to oppose him. The LORD rebuked Satan. Joshua's filthy clothes were taken away, his sin was taken from him, and a clean mitre was set on his head.
key_moments.title: Given Clean Clothes in a Vision

key_moments.description: The LORD told Zechariah to make crowns of gold and silver and set them on Joshua's head. He spoke of a man called The BRANCH, who would build the LORD's temple and rule on his throne.
key_moments.title: Crowned as a Sign

name: Joshua
summary: Joshua, the son of Josedech, was the high priest when the people came back from captivity to Jerusalem. With Zerubbabel he rebuilt the altar and the house of the LORD, and in Zechariah's visions the LORD took away his filthy clothes and had crowns set on his head.

key_moments.description: Jephthah's brothers drove him out because his mother was a harlot. He went to live in the land of Tob, and worthless men gathered to him.
key_moments.title: Driven Out by His Brothers

key_moments.description: When Ammon made war on Israel, the elders of Gilead came for Jephthah. He agreed to lead them if the LORD gave him victory, and they made him their head.
key_moments.title: Called Home to Lead Gilead

key_moments.description: The Spirit of the LORD came on Jephthah, and he vowed to offer to the LORD whatever first came out of his house to meet him. The LORD gave the children of Ammon into his hands.
key_moments.title: Makes a Vow Before the Battle

key_moments.description: His only child, his daughter, came out dancing with timbrels to meet him, and he tore his clothes. She asked for two months to mourn with her friends, then he did to her as he had vowed.
key_moments.title: His Daughter Comes to Meet Him

key_moments.description: When the men of Ephraim came against him, Jephthah fought them. The men of Gilead held the fords of the Jordan, and anyone who said Sibboleth instead of Shibboleth was killed.
key_moments.title: Defeats Ephraim at the Jordan Fords

name: Jephthah
summary: A mighty man of valour from Gilead, driven out by his brothers and later called back to lead his people against Ammon. A vow he made before the battle fell on his only child, his daughter.

key_moments.description: When Abimelech killed the sons of Gideon on one stone, Jotham, the youngest, hid himself and was left alive.
key_moments.title: Escaped by Hiding

key_moments.description: Jotham stood on Mount Gerizim and told how the trees asked the olive, the fig and the vine to be king, and all refused, but the bramble agreed. He warned that fire would come out of Abimelech and Shechem to burn up each other, then fled.
key_moments.title: Warns Shechem with the Parable of the Trees

key_moments.description: God paid back Abimelech for killing his brothers, and the evil of the men of Shechem fell on their own heads. So Jotham's curse came upon them.
key_moments.title: His Curse Comes True

name: Jotham
summary: The youngest son of Gideon, the only one to escape when Abimelech killed his brothers. From Mount Gerizim he told a parable of the trees that warned Shechem what its new king would bring.

key_moments.description: Abimelech won over his mother's family at Shechem and used their silver to hire worthless men. He killed his brothers on one stone at Ophrah, and only the youngest, Jotham, escaped by hiding. Then the men of Shechem made Abimelech king.
key_moments.title: Made King at Shechem

key_moments.description: After three years God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem, and they rose against him. He took the city, sowed it with salt, and burned the tower where about a thousand men and women had fled.
key_moments.title: Shechem Turns Against Him

key_moments.description: As Abimelech came to burn the tower of Thebez, a woman threw a piece of millstone on his head. He told his armourbearer to kill him so no one would say a woman slew him.
key_moments.title: Struck by a Millstone

name: Abimelech
summary: A son of Gideon who killed his seventy brothers to make himself king at Shechem. He reigned three years before God sent trouble between him and the men of Shechem, and he died at Thebez.

key_moments.description: As David fled, Shimei came out cursing him and throwing stones and dust. When Abishai wanted to kill him, David told him to leave Shimei alone, for the LORD had bidden him to curse.
key_moments.title: Cursing the King

key_moments.description: When David came back over the Jordan, Shimei hurried down to meet him, fell down before him and confessed his sin. David swore to him that he would not die.
key_moments.title: Begging for Mercy

key_moments.description: Solomon told Shimei to live in Jerusalem and never go out of it, or he would die. After three years Shimei went to Gath after two runaway servants, and Solomon had him put to death.
key_moments.title: Put to Death for Leaving Jerusalem

name: Shimei
summary: A man of Saul's family from Bahurim who cursed David as he fled from Absalom. David spared him, but Solomon later put him to death for breaking his oath.

key_moments.description: Shepherds drove Zipporah and her six sisters away from the well, but Moses stood up and helped them water their father's flock. Their father took Moses in and gave him Zipporah, and she bore him a son, Gershom.
key_moments.title: Given to Moses as His Wife

key_moments.description: At the inn on the road to Egypt, the LORD met him and sought to kill him. Zipporah took a sharp stone, cut off her son's foreskin, and said, A bloody husband art thou to me. So the LORD let him go.
key_moments.title: Circumcises Her Son on the Way

key_moments.description: Moses had sent Zipporah back to her father. After the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt, Jethro brought her and her two sons to Moses in the wilderness at the mount of God.
key_moments.title: Brought Back to Moses by Jethro

name: Zipporah
summary: A daughter of the priest of Midian, given to Moses as his wife after he helped her and her sisters at a well. On the way to Egypt she circumcised her son when the LORD met him and sought to kill him.

key_moments.description: The LORD sent Samuel to Bethlehem, telling him the LORD looks on the heart. Jesse's youngest son David was brought in from the sheep, Samuel anointed him, and the Spirit of the LORD came upon him.
key_moments.title: Anointed by Samuel

key_moments.description: David came to the camp and heard Goliath mock the armies of God. He went out with a sling and five stones, saying the battle was the LORD's, and struck the Philistine in the forehead with a stone.
key_moments.title: Kills Goliath

key_moments.description: In a cave near Engedi, David cut off a piece of Saul's robe but would not harm him, because Saul was the LORD's anointed. Saul wept and said David would surely be king.
key_moments.title: Sparing Saul's Life

key_moments.description: All the tribes came to David at Hebron and anointed him king over Israel. He took the stronghold of Zion, which became the city of David, and reigned forty years in all.
key_moments.title: Made King over All Israel

key_moments.description: David took Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah, and had Uriah put where he would die in battle. The prophet Nathan told him a story of a stolen lamb and showed him the man was David, and David confessed his sin against the LORD.
key_moments.title: Rebuked by Nathan for Taking Bathsheba

name: David
summary: A shepherd from Bethlehem whom the LORD chose to be king of Israel. He killed Goliath, spared Saul when he could have killed him, and reigned forty years from Hebron and Jerusalem.

key_moments.description: A young prophet sent by Elisha took Jehu into an inner room at Ramoth-gilead and anointed him with oil, saying the LORD had made him king over Israel. His fellow captains blew trumpets and cried that Jehu was king.
key_moments.title: Anointed in Secret

key_moments.description: Jehu raced his chariot to Jezreel so wildly that the watchman knew who it was. When King Joram came out to meet him, Jehu shot him through the heart.
key_moments.title: Drives to Jezreel and Shoots Joram

key_moments.description: At Jezreel, Jehu called to the servants at a window, and they threw Jezebel down. Later, when her body was looked for, almost nothing was left, as the LORD had said through Elijah.
key_moments.title: Has Jezebel Thrown Down

key_moments.description: Jehu called everyone who worshipped Baal to a great sacrifice in Baal's temple, then had his guards kill them. Baal's temple and image were broken down.
key_moments.title: Wipes Out Baal's Worshippers

key_moments.description: The LORD promised that Jehu's sons would sit on Israel's throne to the fourth generation. Yet Jehu took no care to follow the LORD's law wholeheartedly, and he kept the golden calves at Bethel and Dan.
key_moments.title: Keeps the Golden Calves

name: Jehu
summary: An army captain anointed king over Israel to wipe out Ahab's family line. He wiped Baal worship out of Israel, but kept the golden calves at Bethel and Dan.

key_moments.description: Benaiah killed two lionlike men of Moab, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion. He also killed an Egyptian with the Egyptian's own spear.
key_moments.title: Kills a Lion in a Pit

key_moments.description: Benaiah answered King David with an amen. With Zadok and Nathan he brought Solomon down to Gihon to be anointed king.
key_moments.title: Bringing Solomon to Gihon

key_moments.description: At Solomon's command Benaiah put Joab to death at the altar of the LORD. Solomon then set Benaiah over the army in Joab's place.
key_moments.title: Puts Joab to Death

name: Benaiah
summary: A mighty man of David from Kabzeel, set over the Cherethites and the Pelethites. He stood with Solomon and became captain over the whole army.

key_moments.description: Ezra traveled from Babylon to Jerusalem, and the king gave him all he asked, for the LORD's hand was on him. He had made up his mind to study the LORD's law, keep it, and teach it.
key_moments.title: Goes Up from Babylon

key_moments.description: Ezra prayed and confessed, weeping and lying face down before God's house, and a great crowd gathered and wept too. They agreed to put away the foreign wives they had taken, and Ezra made the leaders swear to it.
key_moments.title: Weeping Before God's House

key_moments.description: The people gathered by the Water Gate and asked Ezra to bring out Moses' book of the law. He stood on a wooden pulpit and read from morning until midday, while the Levites helped the people understand.
key_moments.title: Reading the Law

key_moments.description: The people wept on hearing the law, but Nehemiah, Ezra and the Levites told them not to mourn, for the day was holy to the LORD. Gladness in the LORD would be their strength, so they went to eat, drink and share.
key_moments.title: Tells the People Not to Mourn

name: Ezra
summary: Ezra was a priest and a scribe, skilled in the law of Moses, who traveled from Babylon to Jerusalem. He made up his mind to study the LORD's law, keep it, and teach it in Israel.

key_moments.description: David defeated Hadarezer king of Zobah and the Syrians of Damascus who came to help him. He took the shields of gold from Hadarezer's servants to Jerusalem, and much brass from his cities.
key_moments.title: Defeated by David

key_moments.description: Hadarezer brought out the Syrians from beyond the river, and they came to Helam under his captain Shobach. David defeated them, and the kings who served Hadarezer made peace with Israel.
key_moments.title: Defeated Again at Helam

name: Hadarezer
summary: The son of Rehob and king of Zobah, who fought against David. David defeated him twice, and the kings who served him made peace with Israel.

key_moments.description: Samuel came to Bethlehem and had Jesse bring his sons before him, but the LORD chose none of the seven. Jesse sent for the youngest, David, who was keeping the sheep, and Samuel anointed him.
key_moments.title: His Sons Pass Before Samuel

key_moments.description: King Saul sent word to Jesse asking for his son David. Jesse sent David with a donkey loaded with bread, a bottle of wine and a young goat.
key_moments.title: Sending David to Saul

key_moments.description: Jesse was an old man, and his three eldest sons had gone to fight with Saul. He sent David with grain and loaves for his brothers and cheeses for their captain.
key_moments.title: Sends David with Food for His Brothers

name: Jesse
summary: A man of Bethlehem, the grandson of Ruth and Boaz, and the father of eight sons. The LORD chose his youngest, David, to be king.

key_moments.description: Belshazzar threw a great feast for a thousand lords and had the gold and silver cups from the temple in Jerusalem brought in. They drank wine from them and praised gods of gold, silver, wood and stone.
key_moments.title: Drinks from the Temple Cups

key_moments.description: The fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the palace wall. The king shook with fear, and none of his wise men could read the words.
key_moments.title: Sees the Writing on the Wall

key_moments.description: Daniel told Belshazzar he had not humbled his heart, and read the writing: God had numbered his kingdom and ended it, and it would be given to the Medes and Persians. Belshazzar still clothed Daniel in scarlet and made him third ruler.
key_moments.title: Weighed and Found Wanting

key_moments.description: That same night Belshazzar, king of the Chaldeans, was killed, and Darius the Median took the kingdom.
key_moments.title: Slain That Night

name: Belshazzar
summary: A king of Babylon who held a great feast and drank from the holy cups taken from God's temple in Jerusalem. A hand wrote a message on his wall, Daniel read it as God's judgment, and he was killed that same night.

key_moments.description: Elijah found Elisha plowing behind twelve pairs of oxen and threw his cloak over him. Elisha killed his oxen to feed the people, then went after Elijah to serve him.
key_moments.title: Called from the Plow

key_moments.description: Elisha asked that a double share of Elijah's spirit be on him, and he saw Elijah taken up. Then he struck the Jordan with Elijah's mantle, and the waters parted for him.
key_moments.title: Asks for a Double Portion

key_moments.description: Elisha promised a kind woman of Shunem that she would have a son, which came true. When the boy later died, Elisha prayed and stretched himself over the child until the boy sneezed and opened his eyes.
key_moments.title: Raises the Shunammite's Son

key_moments.description: When a Syrian army surrounded Dothan, Elisha prayed and his frightened servant saw fiery horses and chariots filling the mountain. The LORD struck the Syrians blind, and Elisha led them into Samaria, where they were fed and sent home.
key_moments.title: Surrounded by Chariots of Fire

key_moments.description: After Elisha died and was buried, a dead man was thrown into his grave. When the body touched Elisha's bones, the man came back to life and stood up.
key_moments.title: His Bones Bring a Dead Man to Life

name: Elisha
summary: The son of Shaphat who followed Elijah and took his place as prophet in Israel. Through him the LORD healed, fed and protected His people, and even his bones gave a dead man life.

key_moments.description: When the book of the law was found, King Josiah sent Ahikam, Hilkiah the priest and others to ask the LORD what it meant for Judah. They went to Huldah the prophetess, who lived in Jerusalem.
key_moments.title: Sent to Huldah the Prophetess

key_moments.description: King Jehoiakim had the prophet Urijah brought back from Egypt and killed for speaking against the city. But Ahikam was on Jeremiah's side, so Jeremiah was not given to the people to be put to death.
key_moments.title: Standing by Jeremiah

name: Ahikam
summary: Ahikam son of Shaphan was one of the men King Josiah sent to ask of the LORD about the book of the law that had been found. Later he stood by the prophet Jeremiah, so that Jeremiah was not handed over to be killed.

key_moments.description: King Josiah sent his scribe to Hilkiah to count the money for repairing the temple. Hilkiah told Shaphan he had discovered the book of the law inside the LORD's house, and gave it to him to read.
key_moments.title: Finds the Book of the Law

key_moments.description: When the king heard the book read, he sent Hilkiah and others to ask the LORD about it. They went to Huldah the prophetess, who lived in Jerusalem.
key_moments.title: Asking Huldah

key_moments.description: The king had Hilkiah and the priests bring from the temple every vessel made for Baal or other false worship. They were burned in the Kidron fields outside Jerusalem.
key_moments.title: Clears Baal's Vessels from the Temple

name: Hilkiah
summary: The high priest in the days of King Josiah. While the temple was being repaired, he discovered the book of the law inside the LORD's house.

key_moments.description: In Shushan the palace, Nehemiah heard that the people left in Judah were in great trouble and the wall of Jerusalem was broken down. For days he wept, mourned and fasted, and he prayed to the God of heaven.
key_moments.title: Weeping for Jerusalem

key_moments.description: As he served wine to King Artaxerxes, the king saw that he was sad and asked what he wanted. Nehemiah prayed, then asked to be sent to build the city, and the king gave him letters and timber.
key_moments.title: Asks the King to Send Him

key_moments.description: The builders completed the wall in fifty-two days. When their enemies heard of it, they lost heart, for they saw that God had done this work.
key_moments.title: Finishes the Wall in Fifty-Two Days

key_moments.description: When the people wept at hearing the law, Nehemiah, Ezra and the Levites told them not to mourn, for the day was holy to the LORD. They were sent to feast and share, for gladness in the LORD would be their strength.
key_moments.title: Tells the People Not to Mourn

name: Nehemiah
summary: Nehemiah son of Hachaliah served King Artaxerxes in Shushan the palace. When he heard that the wall of Jerusalem was broken down, he went there as governor and led the people to build it again.

key_moments.description: When Stephen was stoned, the witnesses laid their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul, who agreed with his death. Then Saul tore through the church, going into house after house and dragging men and women off to prison.
key_moments.title: Persecuting the Church

key_moments.description: Near Damascus a light shone from heaven around Saul, and Jesus asked him why he was persecuting Him. Saul was blind for three days, until Ananias laid hands on him; then he could see again and was baptized.
key_moments.title: Meets Jesus on the Road to Damascus

key_moments.description: After Paul cast a spirit out of a fortune-telling girl, her masters had Paul and Silas beaten and locked in the stocks. At midnight they prayed and sang praises to God, and after an earthquake the jailer and his whole household believed and were baptized.
key_moments.title: Singing in Prison

key_moments.description: In a great storm at sea, Paul told the crew that an angel of God had promised not one of them would lose his life. The ship broke apart, but everyone reached land safely on the island of Melita.
key_moments.title: Shipwrecked on the Way to Rome

key_moments.description: In Rome Paul was allowed to live by himself with a soldier guarding him. For two whole years he welcomed all who came to his rented house and boldly preached God's kingdom and the Lord Jesus Christ.
key_moments.title: Preaching in Rome

name: Paul
summary: A man from Tarsus, first called Saul, who attacked the church until Jesus spoke to him on the road to Damascus. He became an apostle who carried the gospel to the Gentiles in many lands and wrote many letters to the churches.

key_moments.description: Mary gave birth to Jesus in Bethlehem and laid Him in a manger, because there was no room in the inn. An angel told shepherds that a Saviour was born, Christ the Lord, and they hurried to find Him.
key_moments.title: Born and Laid in a Manger

key_moments.description: Jesus came to John at the Jordan to be baptized. As He came up out of the water, the Spirit of God came down on Him like a dove, and a voice from heaven called Him a beloved Son.
key_moments.title: Baptized in the Jordan

key_moments.description: A boy had five barley loaves and two small fish. Jesus gave thanks and shared them out until about five thousand men were full, and twelve baskets of leftovers were gathered.
key_moments.title: Feeding Five Thousand

key_moments.description: Jesus was crucified between two criminals and asked the Father to forgive them. He promised one of the criminals paradise, then gave His spirit into the Father's hands and died.
key_moments.title: Crucified at Calvary

key_moments.description: Early on the first day of the week, women found the stone rolled away and the body of Jesus gone. Two men in shining clothes told them He was not there but was risen, just as He had said.
key_moments.title: Risen From the Dead

name: Jesus Christ
summary: Born in Bethlehem, Jesus is the One an angel announced as a Saviour, Christ the Lord, and a voice from heaven called Him a beloved Son. He taught, healed and fed the crowds, was crucified, and on the third day He rose from the dead.
